name: Familial Dysfibrinogenemia

criteria.description: Prolonged thrombin time and abnormal clotting assays despite normal fibrinogen antigen levels
Identification of pathogenic mutations in fibrinogen genes (FGA, FGB, or FGG)
Positive family history of bleeding or thrombotic disorders consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of mucocutaneous bleeding or abnormal bleeding tendency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal coagulation tests with genetic confirmation of fibrinogen gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acquired causes of dysfibrinogenemia.

laboratory: Discrepancy between fibrinogen antigen and functional assays
Abnormal clot structure on electron microscopy
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI may detect deep vein thrombosis or hemarthrosis
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in adulthood with underlying liver disease or malignancy
Reversible with treatment of underlying condition
Reduced fibrinogen levels rather than dysfunctional fibrinogen
Bleeding severity correlates with fibrinogen concentration

redFlags: Recurrent thrombotic events despite bleeding tendency
Family history of unexplained bleeding or thrombosis
references: Mannucci PM, et al. Congenital dysfibrinogenemia: clinical features and molecular basis. Blood. 2013.
George JN. Disorders of fibrinogen. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2006.
